title: Split a restaurant bill so the parts add up to the total
examObjective: Predicting the result of core DataWeave functions
basics: `floor(x)` rounds down to a whole number. `a mod b` is the remainder after dividing a by b: `10 mod 3` is 1. Working in whole cents avoids fractions of a cent altogether.
prompt:
A payments app splits a bill evenly between `people` diners. The bill `total` is in cents. Return an array with one amount per diner, in cents, that adds up to exactly `total`.

When it does not divide evenly, the leftover cents go one each to the first diners in the list.
hints: Everyone gets the whole-cent share. Some people get one cent more.
How many cents are left over? `total mod people`.
Build the list with a range `(0 to people - 1)` and give 1 extra cent to each position lower than the remainder.

mustFail.why: rounds each share, so the parts do not add up to the total
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
(0 to payload.people - 1) map round(payload.total / payload.people)

mustFail.why: gives the leftover cents to the last diners instead of the first

explanation.approach: Rounding each share independently cannot guarantee the total: 1000 split three ways rounds to 333 three times, and a cent disappears. Take the whole-cent share for everyone, count what is left with `mod`, and hand those cents out one at a time.

snippets.label: Rounding each share
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
sum((0 to 2) map round(1000 / 3))

snippets.label: Share and remainder
snippets.note: Three shares of 333 and one cent over.

snippets.label: A range as a counter
snippets.note: One element per diner, numbered from 0.
